headline: A Dutch university's AI-controlled racing drone beat three former human world champions at a race in Abu Dhabi, and the study behind it has now been published.
score_reason: Lowered from 7: the race was in Nov 2025 and only the Science Robotics paper is new today; 'first' is the team's own claim.
importance_line: A new peer-reviewed paper shows a small drone beating top human pilots outside a lab, which matters for future robots and vehicles that must move safely in the real world, though the 'first' is the team's own claim.
summary: Popular Science reports that MonoRace, an AI-piloted drone built at the Delft University of Technology in the Netherlands, won the Abu Dhabi Autonomous Racing League in November 2025 with a time better than three former human world champions, and that the team published the details in Science Robotics on 14 Oct 2026. The drone flies at about 62 miles per hour using a camera and a small onboard computer, and the researchers call it the first AI-piloted drone to beat humans in an international race, a claim that rests on the team itself.
freshness: FOLLOW-UP of Nov 2025 race; study published 14 Oct 2026
notes: Race itself is from Nov 2025; the paper is new today.
